newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may change Wednesday T-bill auction terms.
newsitem.headline: Russia may change Wednesday T-bill auction terms.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry will change the terms of Wednesday's Treasury bills auction if the Justice Ministry does not clarify new government securities taxation by then, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

The Finance Ministry will cancel the auction of new T-bill issues planned for Wednesday and replace them with new tranches of old issues, Bella Zlatkis, head of the securities department told Reuters.
The new regulation levies a tax on profits from government securities, which are now tax-exempt.
The new tax imposes the usual profits tax, which is 43 percent for banks and 35 percent for other companies, on government securities, while setting a 15 percent rate on interest from bond coupons.
The Finance Ministry has asked the Justice Ministry to define earnings from discounts on T-bills as interest, rather than profits.
A Justice Ministry official said it was difficult to say whether the ministry would manage to register the regulation before Wednesday.
"We are still working on it -- we are agreeing on the text with the Finance Ministry, State Tax Office and are correcting things which do not correspond to the law," she said.
The Finance Ministry plans to offer 11 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills (series 22069 and 22070) on Wednesday.

The Finance Ministry has already cancelled government paper auctions twice, replacing them with new tranches of old issues, which are not subject to the new tax, due to a lack of clarity on the tax issue.
